commands.name: compile-map
commands.purpose: Builds a custom Skate map into a native Frostbite Patch staging folder. Input is a .blend or .fbx scene (it runs Blender headless with Studio's Native\Blender\studio_map_import.py to make a normalized map export first) or an already normalized map folder (one holding map.json). It can also merge enabled .fbmod files into the same Patch and, with --deploy, install the result into <game>\Mods.

args.name: game-root
args.meaning: Skate install folder. Read for indexing and donor assets. Written to only with --deploy (into Mods).

args.name: map
args.meaning: A .blend/.fbx scene, or a normalized map folder containing map.json. The map ID comes from the scene file name (discmap.blend becomes level dingolevel_reskate_discmap).
args.values: path; a missing file gives 'map scene was not found: <path>'

args.name: staging-root
args.meaning: Output staging folder. Created if missing. Rebuilding into a folder Studio already owns works. A non-empty folder without the .reskate-studio-staging marker is refused.

args.name: enabled.fbmod ...
args.meaning: Any further non-flag arguments are treated as .fbmod files to merge into the Patch (reported as included-mods / conflicts). Unknown flags such as --bogus land here too and fail with 'could not open binary input' late in the run.

args.name: --deploy
args.meaning: Install the staged Patch into <game>\Mods. NOT RUN (safety rule). Its checks, per strings: Skate.exe SHA-256 must match the build, staging and game must be separate trees, refuses a Mods folder not managed by Studio, writes reskate-levels.json and a deployment receipt.

args.name: --mod-folder
args.meaning: Name of the Mods subfolder for --deploy. Without --deploy it is accepted and ignored: '.bad' was not rejected. The name rule from strings is 1-64 letters, digits, spaces, '_', '-' or '.', not starting with '.'.
args.values: name; missing value gives '--mod-folder requires a name'

args.name: --blender
args.meaning: Path to blender.exe for .blend/.fbx input. Optional: it auto-found Blender 5.2 under C:\Program Files\Blender Foundation. Without it and without the RESKATE_BLENDER env var, a missing Blender fails with 'Blender was not found; pass --blender <path to blender.exe> or set RESKATE_BLENDER'.

args.name: --pause-map
args.meaning: Pause-menu map render style, passed through to the Blender converter
args.values: 2d|3d (converter default 3d); anything else gives '--pause-map requires 2d or 3d'

args.name: --time-of-day
args.meaning: Starting or fixed time of day
args.values: morning|noon|afternoon|evening|night; others give 'unknown time of day <x>' (exit 1, checked immediately)

args.name: --stream / --no-stream
args.meaning: Stream render meshes through WorldPartition cells or keep them resident. Default appears to be no streaming for a tiny map (render-cells=0).

args.name: --cell-size
args.meaning: Streaming cell size in metres
args.values: 200|100|50. The prefilter only checks that a value is present; 75 failed late (after export and about 5 s) with 'streaming cell size must be 200, 100 or 50 metres'

args.name: --cell-load-distance
args.meaning: Cell load distance in metres

args.name: --vista-ratio
args.meaning: Vista proxy simplification ratio

args.name: --vista-error
args.meaning: Vista proxy error in metres

args.name: --no-lods
args.meaning: Disable mesh LOD generation

args.name: --lod-ratios
args.meaning: LOD triangle ratios
args.values: comma-separated numbers. A count that differs from --lod-distances only warns: 'using the first N of each'

args.name: --lod-distances
args.meaning: LOD switch distances in metres

args.name: --lod-min-triangles
args.meaning: Minimum triangles for a mesh to get LODs

args.name: --no-gi
args.meaning: Disable baked GI probes

args.name: --enlighten
args.meaning: Build Enlighten probes and input systems (warns 'experimental')

args.name: --enlighten-open-sky
args.meaning: Enlighten open-sky mode. Found in strings, not in the usage line. Accepted in a real run.

args.name: --gi-enlighten-spacing
args.meaning: Enlighten probe spacing in metres (4 gave a 10x2x10 grid on a 40 m map)

args.name: --gi-enlighten-gain
args.meaning: Enlighten gain. Found in strings, not in the usage line. Accepted.

args.name: --no-auto-reflection
args.meaning: Do not auto-place reflection probes

args.name: --bam-lighting / --no-bam-lighting
args.meaning: Include or exclude BAM's Lighting_Global for live time-of-day swaps. Including it is the default and warns that it ships without Enlighten for every level while installed. --bam-lighting is only in strings.

args.name: --no-live-tod
args.meaning: Disable live time-of-day swapping

args.name: --gi-intensity / --gi-rays / --gi-sky / --gi-sun / --gi-bounce
args.meaning: GI bake tuning: intensity factor, ray count, sky lux, sun lux, bounce factor
args.values: number; a missing value gives '<flag> requires a value'

args.name: --gi-lods
args.meaning: GI LOD count
args.values: 1-4 per usage, but 7 was accepted without error (the test map had gi-cells=0)

args.name: --gi-sun-rotation
args.meaning: Sun rotation for the GI bake
args.values: x,y degrees; '30' gives '--gi-sun-rotation takes x,y degrees' (exit 1, checked immediately)

commands.output: stderr carries progress. For .blend input it first prints 'blender=<path>' and 'export=%TEMP%\ReSkateStudio\MapExport\<id>', then '[export NN%] ...' lines from Blender, written with no newline between some, then '[export] finished in Xs'. Next come timestamped steps '[0.0s] Reading normalized map export', 'Indexing native game assets', 'Checking Skate.exe SHA-256', about 245 'Slicing pause-map tile i of 245' lines, the staged bundle names, '[N s] done', and 'warning: ...' lines. stdout on success is key=value: toc=, cas=, layout= (staged paths), triangles, render-cells, vista-cells, lod-meshes, lod-triangles, vista-triangles, lights, tod-lights, collision-resources, collision-stream-bundles, shadow-profile-bundles/assets/components, ebx, resources, chunks, gi-cells, gi-probes, included-mods, conflicts (and deployed= with --deploy, per strings). Errors are a single stderr line.
commands.writes: <staging-root>\.reskate-studio-staging (marker 'ReSkate Studio staging v1') and <staging-root>\Patch\ containing initfs_win32, layout.toc, .reskate-studio-patch (records skate_sha256), reskate-build.json ({schema, tool, version 1.0.0, built, map}), reskate-levels.json (level asset, displayName, startPoints), Win32\globals.toc, Win32\levels\game\dingolevel_reskate_<id>\*.toc, Win32\levels\game\dingolevel_root\dingolevel_root.toc and Win32\configurations\layout\{default,initial}installpackage\cas_01.cas (about 20 MB total for a cube on a plane). Also: a temporary %TEMP%\ReSkateStudio\MapExport\<id>\ that is deleted afterwards, leaving <id>.performance.json; the cache %TEMP%\ReSkateStudio\Cache\<skate-sha256>\map-donors-*.tsv; and, seen after .blend-input runs, assets\<id>\export\map.png and map_clouds.png under the current working directory. With --deploy it also writes <game>\Mods\<folder> (not exercised).
commands.verified: ran-successfully. Real runs on DA-PC, all WITHOUT --deploy, with staging under C:\dev\studio-plus-discovery\map: a .blend from Blender 5.2 (plane, cube, 'spawn' empty), exit 0 in 11.6 s; the normalized folder as input with --no-stream --time-of-day night --no-gi --no-lods --mod-folder, exit 0 in 8.5 s; a long flag set including --stream --cell-size 50 --enlighten --enlighten-open-sky --bam-lighting --gi-enlighten-gain and LOD/vista options, exit 0. Error cases run: bad time of day, cell size 75, unknown flag, missing input, missing fbmod, foreign non-empty staging, mismatched LOD counts, bad sun rotation. --deploy was never run; its behaviour comes from strings only.
commands.example: reskate_cli compile-map "C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Skate" C:\dev\studio-plus-discovery\map\discmap.blend C:\dev\studio-plus-discovery\map\pkg1 --blender "C:\Program Files\Blender Foundation\Blender 5.2\blender.exe"
commands.exit_codes: 0 success; 1 any error (bad option value, missing input, foreign staging, unreadable fbmod, late cell-size failure); 2 generic usage when fewer than 3 positionals are given
commands.runtime: About 8-9 s from a normalized folder and about 11-12 s from a .blend for a trivial map (Blender export about 3 s, game indexing about 2 s, pause-map slicing about 4 s). Real maps will take much longer.
commands.notes: Validation timing matters for a wrapper. --time-of-day, --pause-map and --gi-sun-rotation format errors fail instantly. The --cell-size value, unknown flags and missing fbmods only fail after the full export and authoring (8-11 s), so ReSkate Studio+ should validate these itself first. Failed late runs did not create the staging folder when it did not already exist. When a .blend is given, the CLI calls Blender with studio_map_import.py from <cli dir>\Native\Blender ('Studio's Blender converter (studio_map_import.py) was not found near reskate_cli' otherwise). It also accepts the env var RESKATE_BLENDER and appears to read RESKATE_MAP_PROGRESS JSON lines from the converter. The Studio GUI calls Blender directly: blender --background --factory-startup --disable-autoexec --python studio_map_import.py -- --input X --output Y --map-id ID --map-name NAME --pause-map 2d|3d --timeout-seconds N (other converter options: --scale, --bake-size, --no-procedural-bake). It then passes the normalized folder to compile-map. Build Skate Map.bat uses: compile-map "<game>" "<blend>" "%USERPROFILE%\Desktop\<name>_package" --deploy, and waits while Skate.exe is running.

commands.name: map
commands.purpose: Validates and summarises a normalized map export folder (the folder holding map.json, meshes\, collision\, textures\ and ui\ that the Blender converter produces). Read-only inspection.

args.name: normalized-map-dir
args.meaning: Folder containing map.json. It is not a game root: giving the game root fails with 'could not open <root>\map.json'.

commands.output: stdout key=value: name, objects, materials, glb-files, vertices, triangles, collision-objects, collision-triangles, collision-resources, collision-parts, unique-collision-files, unique-collision-triangles. Errors on stderr, for example 'normalized map directory does not exist', 'could not open <dir>\map.json', and many map.json schema messages from strings: 'map.json must use Y-up coordinates', 'map asset is missing: ', 'map object transform must contain 12 numbers', and so on.
commands.verified: ran-successfully. Ran on C:\dev\studio-plus-discovery\map\norm\discmap, produced by running studio_map_import.py in Blender 5.2: exit 0 with name=discmap objects=8 materials=1 glb-files=10 vertices=156 triangles=62 ... Also ran with the game root (exit 1, could not open map.json), with a nonexistent folder (exit 1) and with an extra --verbose (ignored, same output).

args.name: game-root
args.meaning: Skate install folder (read-only)

args.name: level-ebx-asset
args.meaning: Level EBX asset name as listed by 'levels', for example levels/game/bam_levelroot/commlot_piers_02_streetpark_06

commands.output: stdout key=value: placements, unique-meshes, unique-vertices, unique-triangles, expanded-vertices, expanded-triangles, material-variants, resolved-materials, udim-materials, material-warnings, visited-objects, visited-containers, elapsed-seconds. Errors: 'level-preview requires an EBX asset name' (game root only), 'level EBX was not found', 'MeshSet resource is not indexed'.
commands.writes: none observed (no new files in the working directory)
commands.verified: ran-successfully. levels/game/bam_levelroot/commlot_piers_02_streetpark_06 gave exit 0 (placements=360 unique-meshes=30 unique-triangles=11098 expanded-triangles=48312 ...); levels/nope/nope gave exit 1 'level EBX was not found'; the game root alone gave exit 1.

commands.name: levels
commands.purpose: Indexes the game and lists level containers (level, sublevel, layer and schematic EBX assets) with a total count.

args.name: game-root
args.meaning: Skate install folder (read-only)

args.name: display-limit
args.meaning: How many names to print
args.values: unsigned integer, default 20; 0 prints only the count; non-numeric gives 'invalid stoull argument' (exit 1)

commands.output: stdout: one level asset path per line (for example levels/game/bam_levelroot/commlot_piers_02_streetpark_06), in index order, not sorted, then 'level-containers=6084'
commands.verified: ran-successfully: with no limit (20 lines + level-containers=6084), with 5, with 0 (count only), and with 'abc' (exit 1 invalid stoull argument)
commands.exit_codes: 0 ok; 1 bad limit; 2 no path (generic usage)
commands.notes: To get the full list, pass a large limit such as 100000. The error string 'levels accepts an optional display limit' exists, presumably for extra arguments.

commands.name: layout
commands.purpose: Dumps the game's Data\layout.toc (Frostbite layout) as an indented tree: superBundles, fs, install chunk tables, installManifest (installChunks with id, name, installBundle, flags, sizes, language), installGroups, settings and meta ownables.

args.name: game-root
args.meaning: A folder containing Data\layout.toc. Any folder works, for example a fake root holding just Data\layout.toc. Passing the layout.toc file itself fails with 'could not open binary input'. It reads Data\layout.toc and ignored a corrupt Patch\layout.toc placed beside it.

commands.output: stdout: an indented text tree of about 17 KB, for example 'superBundles (24)' / '    name = Win32/buildkititems' / 'fs (1)' / 'head = 625200' / 'installManifest (13)' / '  installChunks (16)' / '      id = 167afc36-...' / 'estimatedSize = 713996' ... / 'meta (1)'
commands.verified: ran-successfully against the real game root, a fake root with copied Data\layout.toc, and a fake root with a corrupt Patch\layout.toc (still exit 0). Passing the toc file path gives exit 1.
commands.exit_codes: 0 ok; 1 cannot open or parse (stderr 'could not open binary input', or layout header errors such as 'layout is missing its Frostbite header'); 2 no path
commands.notes: To inspect a staged Patch layout, point it at a folder whose Data\layout.toc is that file. It does not take the toc path directly, unlike layout-cas and layout-roundtrip.

commands.name: layout-cas
commands.purpose: Decodes the CAS archive tables (layeredInstallChunkFiles and unlayeredInstallChunkFiles) inside a layout.toc file.

args.name: layout.toc
args.meaning: Path to a layout.toc file, not the game root (the game root gives 'could not open binary input')

commands.output: stdout: 'layeredInstallChunkFiles bytes=584' followed by lines '  archive=1 catalog=0x7837152c padding=0x0', then 'unlayeredInstallChunkFiles bytes=72' with the same line format. Error per strings: '<table> is not an 8-byte record table'.
commands.verified: ran-successfully on <game>\Data\layout.toc (read-only) and on a copy. The game root as argument gives exit 1.
commands.exit_codes: 0 ok; 1 cannot open or parse; 2 no path
commands.notes: Useful to check that a staged Patch\layout.toc references the expected cas archives.

commands.name: layout-roundtrip
commands.purpose: Parses a layout.toc and re-encodes it to check that the encoder is lossless; can optionally write the re-encoded file.

args.name: layout.toc
args.meaning: Path to a layout.toc file (a folder gives 'could not open binary input')

args.name: output.toc
args.meaning: If given, the re-encoded layout is written here. Without it nothing is written (verified: the source file was unchanged and no new files appeared).

commands.output: stdout: 'source-bytes=14663', 'encoded-bytes=14663', 'body-identical=true'. Error per strings: 'could not write round-tripped layout'.
commands.writes: Only the optional output file (rt_out.toc, 14663 bytes in the test). Never the input file.
commands.verified: ran-successfully on a copy of Data\layout.toc in C:\dev\studio-plus-discovery\map\fakeroot, with and without an output path. A folder argument gives exit 1.
commands.exit_codes: 0 ok (also when body-identical is false is unknown: not observed); 1 open, parse or write failure; 2 no path
commands.notes: To be safe, always pass a copied input and an output path outside the game root.

commands.name: compile-mod
commands.purpose: Compiles one or more binary .fbmod files against the installed game into a native Frostbite Patch staging folder (Patch/layout.toc, Patch/initfs_win32, Patch/Win32/... CAS archives and level TOCs). This is the build step; deploy-mod then copies the staged build into Mods.

args.name: game-root
args.meaning: Skate install folder. It must contain Skate.exe (SHA-256 hashed and stamped into the build) and the Data folder, and Oodle oo2core_9_win64.dll.

args.name: staging-dir
args.meaning: Output folder. It is created if missing. If it already exists it must be empty or carry the .reskate-studio-staging marker, and then it is wiped and rebuilt. It must be outside the game directory.

args.name: fbmod
args.meaning: One or more binary FBMOD files, applied in order. A .fbproject is rejected ('file is not a binary FBMOD'). Any extra token, such as --verbose, is treated as an FBMOD path and fails with 'could not open binary input'.

commands.output:
On success, three lines on stdout:
resources=3
bundles=6
tocs=6
On failure, one error line (stderr merged), for example: 'compile-mod requires a staging path and at least one FBMOD' (fewer than 3 args after the command), 'could not open <root>\Skate.exe for SHA-256 (Windows 2)', 'file is not a binary FBMOD', 'could not open binary input', 'staging is not empty and is not owned by ReSkate Studio', 'Cosmetic shader parameter dependency is unavailable: <guid>' (a skin-tone-create fbmod failed this way), and from strings 'staging must be a dedicated folder outside the game directory'.
commands.writes: Only <staging-dir>: .reskate-studio-staging (text 'ReSkate Studio staging v1'), Patch\.reskate-studio-patch (text 'ReSkate Studio native Patch v1' plus 'skate_sha256=<hex>'), Patch\initfs_win32 (copied from the game), Patch\layout.toc, Patch\Win32\configurations\layout\{defaultinstallpackage,initialinstallpackage}\cas_01.cas (about 49 MB and 10 MB for a 3-resource animation mod), and Patch\Win32\levels\game\<level>\<level>.toc for bam_levelroot, ftue_island, isle_of_grom, mpr, sdm_int_001 and sdm_int_002. The FBMODs are loaded before staging is touched: a missing FBMOD leaves no folder, but a compile error after that (the skin case) leaves a staging folder containing only the marker. Nothing was written to the game root (file count and newest mtime checked before and after).
commands.verified: ran-successfully: compile-mod <real game root> C:\dev\studio-plus-discovery\mods\out\stage3 out\anim.fbmod (an fbmod made with animation-import from the scooter push_regular_medium.fbx) gave exit 0. Also ran it with the same fbmod twice, re-ran into an existing owned staging folder (wiped and rebuilt, exit 0), and ran the error cases listed under output.
commands.exit_codes: 0 success; 1 any error; 2 when no args follow the command (prints the generic usage)
commands.runtime: about 3 to 4 s for a small animation mod (about 2.7 s of that is the game index load)
commands.notes: No flags found. The build is tied to the exact Skate.exe hash, and deploy-mod refuses it if Skate.exe changes. A skin-tone-create fbmod failed to compile with 'Cosmetic shader parameter dependency is unavailable', so not every fbmod the CLI itself produces will compile. Studio GUI labels from strings: 'Staging folder', 'Staging root containing Patch/layout.toc', 'CurrentProject.fbmod'.

commands.name: deploy-mod
commands.purpose: Installs a compiled staging build into <game-root>\Mods\<mod-folder> as a transaction. It copies the staging Patch folder contents, verifies the copy, backs up any previous version, and writes a deploy receipt database in the game root.

args.name: game-root
args.meaning: Skate install folder. It must contain a Data folder and a Skate.exe whose SHA-256 matches the skate_sha256 recorded in the staging build.

args.name: staging-root
args.meaning: A compile-mod output folder. It must contain Patch/layout.toc and Patch/initfs_win32.

args.name: mod-folder-name
args.meaning: Name of the folder created under <game-root>\Mods. It is a name, not a path.
args.values: 1-64 letters, digits, spaces, '_', '-' or '.', not starting with '.'

commands.output:
On success, five lines:
mod=<game-root>\Mods\<name>
backup=<empty, or <game-root>\.ReSkateStudio-Mod-backup\<name> when a previous copy was replaced>
retired-patch=<empty, or the path of a retired old-style root Patch>
files=11
bytes=64759357
There may also be a 'note: ...' line (from strings). Errors seen: 'deploy-mod requires <game-root> <staging-root> <mod-folder>', 'deploy target does not contain the Skate Data directory', 'staging folder must contain Patch/layout.toc and Patch/initfs_win32', 'mod folder name ".bad" is not usable: 1-64 letters, digits, spaces, '_', '-' or '.', not starting with '.'', 'Skate.exe differs from this staged build; rebuild the mod before deploying'. From strings: 'This staged build has no Skate.exe SHA-256; rebuild it in Studio before deploying', 'staging and game folders must be separate directory trees', 'deployment paths cannot contain symbolic links or junctions: ', 'another ReSkate Studio deployment is already running', '... is not managed by ReSkate Studio; move it out of Mods first', 'refusing to replace ...', 'staged build exceeds the file-count limit', 'staged build contains no files'.
commands.writes: In <game-root>: Mods\<name>\ (a copy of staging\Patch: .reskate-studio-patch, initfs_win32, layout.toc, Win32\...), .ReSkateStudio-last-deploy.db (binary key/value receipt with version, state=Deployed, gameRoot, modRoot, backupRoot, retiredPatch, displacedRoot), and on redeploy .ReSkateStudio-Mod-backup\<name>\ holding the previous copy. Temporary or transaction folders from strings: .ReSkateStudio-Mod-pending-*, .ReSkateStudio-Mod-rollback-*, .ReSkateStudio-Mod-failed-*, .ReSkateStudio-Mod-removed-*, .ReSkateStudio-Patch-backup-*, .ReSkateStudio-Patch-retired-*. It can retire a root Patch folder marked .frosty-managed-skate-patch and uses a mutex named Local\ReSkateStudioPatch_*.
commands.verified: ran-successfully against a FAKE game root only: C:\dev\studio-plus-discovery\mods\fakegame (an empty Data folder plus a copy of Skate.exe). The first deploy and a redeploy (which created the backup) both exited 0. The SHA-mismatch, bad-name, missing-Data and non-staging errors were also triggered with fake roots. It was never run against the real game.
commands.exit_codes: 0 success; 1 any error; 2 with no args (generic usage)
commands.runtime: 0.3 to 0.4 s for about 65 MB (local copy)
commands.notes: The game-root check only looks for a Data folder and a Skate.exe with the matching hash, so a wrapper can test deploys into a fake root. The string 'deploy-patch' sits beside deploy-mod in the strings, but 'reskate_cli deploy-patch' prints the generic usage (exit 2), so it is not a separate command. Related: compile-map has --deploy and --mod-folder <name>, and skin-tone-create has --deploy <mod-folder>; those belong to other commands.
